subject: Cobalt Works: on-prem K8s topology + disk contingency (network/egress/KMS checks)
messages:
From: Alex Gentry <alex@cobaltworks.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Jose Ramirez <jose@cobaltworks.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem deployment - cluster topology and disk contingency

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to kick off the private deployment planning for our primary site in Austin (3 racks, colo provider: LoneStar). Before the kickoff I put together a short list of constraints from our infra/security teams:

- No public IPs assigned to worker nodes; egress must NAT through a perimeter appliance
- All persisted model artifacts must be on encrypted block storage (FDE at rest)
- KMS for key management will be provided by our vault team (TransVault) — we'll need the integration points and allowed IPs
- On-site NFS is available but ops would prefer local NVMe for ephemeral caches
- We expect steady traffic of 25–40 rps with occasional bursts up to 120 rps during business hours

Can you confirm what node pool mix you recommend (control plane sizing, worker profiles for GPU vs CPU, ephemeral vs persistent volumes) and any network egress patterns we should prepare for? Also send any preflight checklist we should review with our networking team.

Appreciate it — cc'ing Jose (ops) to surface any low-level constraints.

—Alex
Alex Gentry
Head of Infrastructure, Cobalt Works

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gentry <alex@cobaltworks.com>
Cc: Jose Ramirez <jose@cobaltworks.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2029 12:33:00 -0400
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment - cluster topology and disk contingency

Thanks Alex — this is helpful context. Attached is our lightweight preflight checklist (redwood-private-deploy-checklist.pdf) and a sketch of the recommended network boundary (network-diagram-v1.png). High-level responses below, followed by a short proposed node-pool matrix and open questions for your TransVault team.

Quick answers
- No public IPs: supported. We recommend NAT at the edge/colo egress appliance with a small set of egress ranges for control-plane callbacks and model update pulls.
- Encrypted block storage: we support FDE and envelope encryption; recommended flow is customer KMS (TransVault) to manage wrapping keys, Redwood uses ephemeral UNSEAL keys on nodes only.
- Local NVMe for ephemeral cache: recommended for model shard caches and KV cache; PVC-backed PVs for model artifacts that must be retained across restarts.
- Expected throughput: design for baseline 40 rps with burst headroom to 150 rps (we do autoscaling + burst policy on Dedicated). We'll size GPU pools for sustained traffic and keep a warm CPU pool for short-lived inference and preprocessing jobs.

Proposed node-pool matrix (initial)
- control-plane: 3x m6i.large (HA control plane, colocated in separate rack switches) — network policy: host-only management VLAN; no GPUs
- gpu-inference: 4x p3-like nodes (32GB GPU mem) — pinned to racks 1 and 2, PVs: local NVMe for cache, optional small encrypted PV on block store for artifacts
- cpu-workers: 6x c6i-type for batching/preproc and canary traffic — use encrypted block volumes for persistent artifacts
- infra-ops: 2x s-utility (smaller) for logging/sidecar and local CI tasks

Storage profile
- Model artifacts (golden): replicated encrypted block store (backed by colo block replication, snapshot schedule daily)
- Ephemeral model caches: local NVMe, backed by an eviction policy for stale shards
- Logs/metrics: central ops tier on infra-ops PVs and forwarded to your SIEM; retention: 90 days by default (can increase)

Network / egress notes
- Control plane callbacks: we will need outbound access to redwood-control.redwood.ai (ports 443) from the control-plane NAT ranges; we can provide an allowlist of IPs once region is selected.
- Model update pulls can be scheduled via an internal pull plane to reduce external egress frequency.
- If you require zero external egress, we can run an air-gapped variant but that adds ~2–3 weeks to onboarding and requires signed images.

Open questions for TransVault (KMS)
1) Preferred key wrap algorithm and whether we will rotate keys on our schedule or defer to your rotation policy
2) IPs/CIDR ranges for TransVault HSM endpoints so we can open egress
3) Is there an automated signing API for node bootstrap (we prefer cert-based bootstrap if available)

Next steps
- Can Jose share a short list of IPs for the colo perimeter NAT appliance and any network ACLs?
- If TransVault can share endpoints, we will draft an integration runbook and a KMS proof-of-concept test plan.
- Internal kickoff: propose Wed Jun 5 (US/Eastern) 10:00–10:45 to walk the checklist and confirm timelines.

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0182

Marissa — thanks, this looks like a good starting point. Quick answers inline:

- NAT appliance IPs: see attached (cobalt-site-lan-updated.drawio) — our perimeter currently NATs to 198.51.100.12/29 for outbound; we'll reserve two additional IPs for control-plane callbacks if needed.
- TransVault endpoints: Jose will follow up but TransVault provides two HSM endpoints in our colo 10.200.5.0/24 (internal) and a public egress endpoint in their managed cloud for cert signing. We'll prefer the internal one if possible.
- Rotation: we rotate master keys quarterly; subordinate keys can be managed by Redwood if you prefer.

Couple of asks before Wed:
1) A quick note on how Redwood will handle node-bootstrap certs (CSR flow or pre-signed tokens) so we can validate with our identity team.
2) Can you confirm the recommended PV snapshot cadence for model artifacts (daily snapshots OK?)

I'll be on the call Wed — Jose will have TransVault on standby.

—Alex

Folks — forwarding Alex's confirm and the TransVault note. Short internal checklist items before the Wed 10:00 call:

1) Karthik: draft the CSR-based bootstrap flow (we will prefer certs over static tokens). Include cert lifetime and rotation trigger (recommend ephemeral node certs 7d).
2) Laura: check snapshot automation options against our block-store adapter; validate that daily snapshots + 7-day retention meets their compliance (they asked for daily). Also confirm restoration SLA — must be able to restore a model artifact within 30 minutes for critical endpoints.
3) Neha: prepare the egress allowlist (we'll provide Redwood control-plane IPs) and confirm whether we can support the internal TransVault endpoint (10.200.5.0/24) over the private link. Flag any firewall/NAT gateway work.

Also, we'll prepare a minimal PoC plan: single control-plane rack, 2 GPU nodes, 2 CPU workers, and a mock KMS wrap/unwrap test. I'll draft the runbook and post to the Drive link in the thread after the call.

Thanks — Marissa
